_note: This eval set is deliberately public-safe. A real 'large monorepo' test case existed during development but described specific, real architectural and security facts about a private codebase (its exact stack, that a DB layer was unused scaffolding, that it had no auth) — that's disclosure, not a generic example, so it was replaced below with a template you fill in against a repo you actually have rights to test against. Eval 2 (autoresearch) is untouched because it targets an already-public GitHub repo (karpathy/autoresearch) with no confidentiality concern.

evals.name: large-monorepo-template
evals.prompt: Onboard me to this repo — I'm a new engineer and need to understand what it does, how it's built, and how it's architected before I start contributing.
evals.expected_output: TEMPLATE — not pre-filled on purpose. Point this eval at a large, multi-language monorepo you have rights to test against (several services/apps, a polyglot stack, ideally with at least one 'thin scaffolding vs. real business logic' seam) and write the real expected_output/expectations for that repo before running it. This slot exists to exercise the skill's fan-out judgment on genuine complexity, which the small autoresearch case below can't test by itself.
expectations: Produces both a Markdown report file and an HTML report file as separate output files
The HTML report's diagram-rendering script tag references a local file (e.g. ./mermaid.min.js), not a CDN URL (e.g. cdn.jsdelivr.net, unpkg.com)

The report includes, at minimum, an executive/business summary, an architecture diagram, a domain model section, a critical workflow walkthrough, and a list of open questions/unknowns for the original developers
The fan-out in Step 2 dispatched more than one research worker, each scoped to a real architectural seam of the substituted repo, rather than one worker per directory or a single unscoped pass
Claims about business intent, users, who pays, or motive are either cited to a specific file/line or explicitly flagged as inferred/unknown
The report cites specific repository file paths (ideally with line numbers) as evidence for its claims, not just general unsourced description
The unknowns/open-questions section is non-empty and specific to the substituted repository (not generic boilerplate)

REPLACE WITH: 1-3 assertions about facts specific to the repo you substitute in (e.g. a real dead-code layer it should catch, a real security posture it should state correctly) — this is where the eval earns its keep, so don't skip it

evals.name: autoresearch-small
evals.prompt: Onboard me to this repo — I'm a new engineer and need to understand what it does, how it's built, and how it's architected before I start contributing.
evals.expected_output: A proportionally short Markdown + self-contained HTML onboarding report that correctly recognizes this as a small, single-purpose local script (not a service), skips or explicitly marks not-applicable any sections that don't fit a system this size (deployment diagram, service dependency diagram, database ERD), and surfaces the real domain-specific findings: the gitignored/untracked results.tsv experiment ledger, and the hard NVIDIA GPU requirement with no CPU fallback.
expectations: Produces both a Markdown report file and an HTML report file as separate output files
The HTML report's diagram-rendering script tag references a local file (e.g. ./mermaid.min.js), not a CDN URL (e.g. cdn.jsdelivr.net, unpkg.com)

The report includes, at minimum, an executive/business summary, an architecture diagram, a domain model section, a critical workflow walkthrough, and a list of open questions/unknowns for the original developers

Claims about business intent, users, who pays, or motive are either cited to a specific file/line or explicitly flagged as inferred/unknown (e.g. with a marker like the warning emoji or the word 'inferred' or 'unknown')
The report cites specific repository file paths (ideally with line numbers) as evidence for its claims, not just general unsourced description
The unknowns/open-questions section is non-empty and specific to this repository (not generic boilerplate that could apply to any codebase)

The report does not force irrelevant enterprise-scale sections (e.g. a fabricated Kubernetes/cloud deployment diagram, or a multi-service dependency diagram) onto what is a single-script local tool — it either omits those sections or explicitly marks them not applicable, and the overall report length is proportionally short rather than padded
The report identifies that the experiment results ledger (results.tsv or equivalent) is untracked/gitignored and not committed to version control
The report identifies that the system requires an NVIDIA GPU with no CPU/alternative-platform fallback in the code
